title: Consumers Report a Higher Likelihood of Applying for Credit

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed released results from its February 2015 SCE Credit Access Survey showing rejection rates declined from 24.2% to 20.0% per applicant, with the most notable change being a drop in credit card limit increase rejections from 38% to 24%. Despite a decrease in the overall proportion likely to apply for credit (32% to 29%), the average likelihood of applying for mortgage refinance doubled from 6% to 12%.
key_points: Rejection rates per applicant declined from 24.2% to 20.0% between October 2014 and February 2015
Credit card limit increase rejection rates fell sharply from 38% to 24%
The lowest creditworthy group saw rejection rates rise to 52.6% (up from 48.7% in October 2014)
Proportion likely to apply for at least one credit type decreased from 32% to 29%
Average likelihood of applying for mortgage refinance doubled from 6% to 12%
For ages 41-59, the mortgage refinance application likelihood jumped from 6% to 15%
why_it_matters: This survey captures consumer credit demand and access conditions but is not directly relevant to market structure or macro catalysts. Credit access data can inform broader consumer financial health assessments, but the 2015 publication date makes this stale for real-time financial analysis.
